can you render as per The black you're seeing isn't coming from your component — your `SceneList` already renders on a transparent `AbsoluteFill` (nothing paints `COLORS.bg`). The black appears because the *render output* defaults to an opaque format. To keep transparency you need to render to a codec + pixel format that has an alpha channel.

Two parts to it:

**1. Make sure nothing paints a background.** You're fine here. Just double-check your `Root`/`<Composition>` and any wrapper above `MainComposition` don't set `backgroundColor`. If something does, remove it.

**2. Render with an alpha-capable codec.** Pick one:

ProRes 4444 (`.mov`, best quality, large files, great for editors like Premiere/After Effects/DaVinci):
```bash
npx remotion render MainComposition out/video.mov \
  --codec=prores --prores-profile=4444 --pixel-format=yuva444p10le
```

WebM with VP8 (`.webm`, much smaller, good for web/overlays):
```bash
npx remotion render MainComposition out/video.webm \
  --codec=vp8 --pixel-format=yuva420p
```

PNG sequence (frames with alpha, if you want maximum flexibility):
```bash
npx remotion render MainComposition out/frames --sequence --image-format=png
```

The key flag is the `yuva...` pixel format — the `a` is the alpha channel. Without it, FFmpeg composites your transparent frames onto black.

If you render programmatically with `renderMedia()`, pass the equivalent options:
```js
await renderMedia({
  composition,
  codec: "prores",
  proResProfile: "4444",
  pixelFormat: "yuva444p10le",
  // ...
});
```

A couple of notes: standard `.mp4`/H.264 cannot hold transparency at all, so there's no flag that makes an MP4 transparent — you have to use one of the formats above. And in Remotion Studio's preview, you can toggle the transparent (checkerboard) background from the settings if you want to see it there too.
